verses.1: And in one year, King Persia heard the words of Jehovah from the mouth of Jeremiah. Jehovah sent a spirit to King Persia, and his word spread throughout all his kingdom. This also was recorded in writing as follows:
verses.2: Thus said Koresh, king of Persia: “All the kings of the earth have given me, O Jehovah, God of the heavens, and he has commanded me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judea.”
verses.3: From among all nations, he will be their God. He will reign over Jerusalem, which is in Judah. He will build the Temple of Jehovah, the God of Israel. This is the God who reigns over Jerusalem.
verses.4: And all those who remain in all the places where he lived, they will be taken away by the people of those places, in exchange for money, gold, treasures, and even animals. This is done so that they can go to the house of God, which is in Jerusalem.
verses.5: And the leaders of the fathers went to Judah, along with Benyamin, the priests, and the Levites. They brought God’s spirit to all the people in that city, so that they could build the Temple of Jehovah in Jerusalem.
verses.6: And all around them, they strengthened their hands with gold and silver vessels. They blessed livestock and fields, for all the offerings they presented.
verses.7: And King Koresh brought out all the utensils of the Temple of God, those that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem. He gave them to his God in his Temple.
verses.8: And King Persia sent his envoy, and they reported to Shechem, the ruler of Judah.
verses.9: And these are the numbers: thirty gold aggarteys, and one thousand silver aggarteys. That makes a total of ninety-five aggarteys.
verses.10: Thirty gold coins, forty silver coins from different years, and twelve other items. In total, one thousand pieces.
verses.11: All the utensils for gold and silver—five thousand and four hundred talents in total—were brought by Shebazzar during the transport of the goods from Babylon to Jerusalem.
